title: fix(runtime): the SQLite file-path refusal names what the operator can change
body:
Fixes #23898

Clause-②: no

## What changes

`sqliteFilenameFromUrl` in `packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts` raises the refusal "`KIND driver was selected but the URL does not look like a file path (WHY).`" Both hosts print it: the standalone host tags it `[StandaloneStack]`, and the CLI's legacy `os serve` path prints it untagged as the fatal `UnsupportedDriverError`. The first clause is unchanged, and so are the rule, the set of refused inputs, the error class, the exit and the scheme-only naming. Only the advice after the first clause changes.

| arm | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `its scheme is "SCHEME"` | `Use file:/path/to/db.sqlite, or set OS_DATABASE_DRIVER explicitly.` | `Use file:/path/to/db.sqlite to keep the KIND driver, or use a driver that matches the URL: unset the driver selection (OS_DATABASE_DRIVER, --database-driver or the databaseDriver option) so the URL selects it, or set the selection to the URL's driver.` |
| `it names no file after "file:"` | `Use file:/path/to/db.sqlite, or set OS_DATABASE_DRIVER explicitly.` | `Name the file after "file:", as in file:/path/to/db.sqlite.` |

**Why each arm gets its own remedy.** The card says this refusal reaches an operator "only under an explicit `sqlite` / `sqlite-wasm` selection". I measured that on the public door, and it holds for the scheme arm but not for the empty-`file:` arm. `OS_DATABASE_URL=file: os serve --dev`, with no driver selected, gets the empty-`file:` refusal on both hosts (table below). A `file:` URL selects the `sqlite` kind on its own, so any driver advice on that arm would send the operator around a loop: unsetting the selection hands the URL straight back to `sqlite`. On that arm the remedy names the file and nothing else. On the scheme arm it carries both options the card's Done-looks-like names. The selection doors are listed and none is assumed, because the kind may have come from `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER` (which `--database-driver` sets), from the `databaseDriver` option, or from the URL.

**CLI host.** It holds no copy of the sentence. `sqliteFileFor` in `packages/cli/src/utils/storage-driver.ts` re-raises the runtime's message with the tag stripped, so the CLI is not edited. `driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts` still holds the two hosts equal (green, below). Its rows carry the WHY fragment, and the whole sentence is held by derivation (`toBe(sentence.replace(...))`) rather than by a literal sentence row, so no remedy row was added there.

## Public door, base `fd0e72abc` vs head `012b45095`

Each case ran from a fresh directory outside the repo with `node packages/cli/bin/run.js serve --dev`. The standalone host cases used a minimal `objectstack.config.ts`. The CLI host cases set `OS_MODE=off` and used a config that declares one object, because the legacy path resolves storage only for a stack that declares objects. Every case exited 1. `PLACEHOLDER` appeared 0 times in every output, and no directory was created in the case directory on either tree.

| case | base: first error line, after the first clause | head: the same |
|---|---|---|
| standalone, `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite`, `jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5999/db` | `(its scheme is "jdbc:"). Use file:/path/to/db.sqlite, or set OS_DATABASE_DRIVER explicitly.` | `(its scheme is "jdbc:"). Use file:/path/to/db.sqlite to keep the sqlite driver, or use a driver that matches the URL: unset ... or set the selection to the URL's driver.` |
| standalone, `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite-wasm`, `postgres://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@127.0.0.1:5999/db` | `(its scheme is "postgres://"). Use file:/path/to/db.sqlite, or set OS_DATABASE_DRIVER explicitly.` | `(its scheme is "postgres://"). Use file:/path/to/db.sqlite to keep the sqlite-wasm driver, or use a driver that matches the URL: ...` |
| CLI legacy (`OS_MODE=off`), the same two | the same, untagged | the same new remedy, untagged |
| standalone and CLI legacy, no selection, `OS_DATABASE_URL=file:` | `(it names no file after "file:"). Use file:/path/to/db.sqlite, or set OS_DATABASE_DRIVER explicitly.` | `(it names no file after "file:"). Name the file after "file:", as in file:/path/to/db.sqlite.` |

Following the new remedy's unset leg for the card's own URL (`OS_DATABASE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5999/db`, no driver) on head exits 1 with `[StandaloneStack] Unsupported database URL scheme "jdbc:". Supported schemes: postgres://, pg://, ...`. So the next refusal names the drivers that exist.

## Tests (head `012b45095`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: exit 0, `Test Files 404 passed (404)`, `Tests 6157 passed | 19 skipped (6176)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2 src/utils/driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts src/utils/storage-driver.test.ts`: exit 0, `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 204 passed (204)`. `@objectstack/runtime` resolves to its `dist/` there, which was rebuilt at head first (`grep -c 'unset the driver selection'` gives 1 in both `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs`).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: exit 0. The runtime's `tsconfig.json` excludes tests. The changed test compiles in the test layer (`check:test-typecheck` OK), and it is not in `test-typecheck-debt.json`.
- New rows in `standalone-stack-explicit-sqlite-non-file-refusal.test.ts` (98 tests in the file, 18 of them new):
  - the scheme arm under both kinds, both doors and two URLs, plus the exported rule;
  - the empty-`file:` arm via `file:` and `FILE:`, with no selection (the `databaseUrl` option and `OS_DATABASE_URL`) and with an explicit `sqlite` selection (both doors).
  - Each row reads the remedy only after checking that the message opens with the unchanged first clause.

## Ablation (one-off, no permanent file)

The fix was committed first. `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` wrote the old remedy back into `standalone-stack.ts`:
- anchor hit 1 time, count 1 to 0; the replacement marker went 0 to 1;
- blob `6ddd65e0af79` to `9d5038cced7e`;
- on-disk counts during the run: marker 1, new remedy 0.

The suite imports `./standalone-stack.js` relatively, so it reads `src/` and no rebuild leg was needed. Result: `Tests 18 failed | 80 passed (98)`. The 18 red rows are exactly the new remedy rows, and the 80 first-clause, credential and control rows stayed green. Restore: blob after restore equals HEAD (`6ddd65e0af79`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Gates (head `012b45095`)

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 62 commands from merge base `9e797a897`. All 62 ran locally, each exit recorded before any pipe.
- `--ran` reconciliation: exit 0, `62 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 60 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED`.
- 60 exited 0.
- NOT MEASURED locally, `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET): it reads built output from packages outside this diff's closure that this checkout has not built. CI runs it on a full build.
- NOT MEASURED locally, `pnpm check:type-check-debt` (exit 3): its own build leg timed out waiting for the shared verify lock. CI runs it.
- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack-explicit-sqlite-non-file-refusal.test.ts`: exit 0, 0 errors and 0 warnings on each file, and neither was ignored. The repo-wide lint run is the PR's `Lint & Repo Gates` check-run.

## Acceptance notes

- **Observation, not filed: the scheme arm is also reachable with no selection.** A `file:` (or `sqlite:`, or `wasm-sqlite://`) prefix that wraps a `SCHEME://` value reaches it. Measured on both trees: `OS_DATABASE_URL=file:postgres://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@127.0.0.1:5999/db` gets `(its scheme is "postgres://")`, with the credentials absent. There the new remedy's first option (a `file:` path) is the fix, and its "unset the driver selection" leg does nothing because nothing was selected. No sentence is false, so this is an observation, not a defect. Carrier: none.
- **The pending `.changeset/23863-explicit-sqlite-non-file-refusal.md` quotes the old remedy** in its "After" sentence. That changeset and this one are both pending, so they ship in the same release, and this changeset's FROM/TO supersedes the quote. It is outside this card's file surface and was not edited.
- `content/`, `skills/` and `docs/` quote neither the first clause nor the remedy (`git grep` count 0 at head). The positive control is the same grep over `packages/`, which hits.
